## Constant gravity and the cell form of the gravity work (`gravity-work: cell`) {#sec-ch06-cell}

### Summary

`const-gravity`[^rg-cf144a647361] is the only gravity snapy has: a constant vector $(g_1, g_2, g_3)$ in m s$^{-2}$, read from the
`forcing`[^rg-f239edda6399] block. It adds $\rho g_a$ to each momentum and $\rho v_ag_a$ to the total energy, in every cell and at
every stage. The $x_1$ part is scaled by the non-hydrostatic factor $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$[^rg-1186f06fe11f] (key `non-hydrostatic`[^rg-40de9bc874ef]); the rest of the
$x_1$ gravity, $(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}})$, is applied through the hydrostatic pressure correction of
@sec-ch05. With `gravity-work: cell` the energy term stays as it is: the work is booked in the cell where the
force acts. That is the simplest choice, and it is the one the key selects away from: `gravity-work`[^rg-72cdee3ac795] defaults to
`face` ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). It is accurate cell by cell; its cost is that it
does not conserve total energy plus potential energy, because the work of the mass crossing a face is booked in
the two neighbouring cells at their own centroids, not where the mass crosses. The gravity-work fixer repairs the
integral of that defect once per step.

Where the planet constants are set: gravity is `forcing/const-gravity/grav1..3` (this section); the rotation rate is
`forcing/coriolis/omega1..3` [s$^{-1}$] (@sec-ch09-coriolis); and there is no planet-radius key: on a
spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grid the radius is $x_1$, so the deck sets it through the bounds
`geometry/bounds/x1min` and `x1max`[^rg-896a4d0cea2b] [m] (@sec-ch03-sphpolar).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Applies constant gravity as a body force and books its work $\rho v_1g_1$ in the same cell, @eq-ch06-cell-work.

**Data.** Reads the stage-start primitives and $(g_1,g_2,g_3)$ [m s$^{-2}$]; adds $\rho g_a$ and $\rho v_ag_a$ in every cell.

**Placement.** Each stage, in the forcing loop of `HydroImpl::forward`; the face part after the $x_1$ flux is final.

**Activation.** `forcing/const-gravity/gravity-work: cell`, set explicitly (default `face`); implies the fixer.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact cell work of the stage state; no exact $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ invariant, @eq-ch06-cell-defect.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch06-cell-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\in[0,1]$ the non-hydrostatic factor (key
`non-hydrostatic`); $G_i=(p^{L}_{i+1/2}-p^{R}_{i-1/2})/\Delta x_{1,i}$ [N m$^{-3}$] the hydrostatic-split pressure force
density of @eq-ch05-hsmode-force (code `rho_grav`); $W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i$[^rg-c40954ec43ff], $W^{\mathrm{face}}_i$[^rg-7c89ae1f45ba] [W m$^{-3}$] and
$F^{\mathrm{ref}}$[^rg-82297cb4f780] as in appendix A; $\mathcal D$[^rg-b660c0a73eb0] [J] the step's $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ defect.

`gravity-work` takes `cell`, `face` or `face-wallc`; any other value is refused when the forcing is read and
again when the hydro module is built from Python. $g_2$ and $g_3$ always book cell work only.

### Derivation

The template of @eq-ch06-dwork-booked says that a scheme conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ exactly when its work satisfies
$W_iV_i = -\dot P_i - \Delta_i[A\phi F]$ for some discrete potential energy $P$. The cell form does not start from
a $P$. It books

$$
\begin{aligned}
W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i &= \alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\,\rho_iv_{1,i}g_1 + (1-\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}})\,v_{1,i}\,G_i ,\\
W_i &= W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i + W^{\mathrm{face}}_i[F-F^{\mathrm{ref}}] ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-cell-work}

where $G_i$ is the hydrostatic-split force density `rho_grav` of @eq-ch05-hsmode-force,
$W^{\mathrm{face}}[\cdot]$ is the face form @eq-ch06-dwork-face evaluated on the flux in brackets, $F$ is the total
$x_1$ mass flux after the positivity limiter and sedimentation and $F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the flux the Riemann
solver returned. The first term is added in `ConstGravityImpl::forward` from `grav1`[^rg-88e66223cc5e]
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward >}})
and, for $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}<1$, the $G_i$ term by the hydrostatic correction, `du[IPR] += dt * w[IVX] * rho_grav *
(1 - non_hydrostatic)`; the second is booked as `gravity_energy_correction`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}),
the face work of the flux minus `bflux1`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
When neither the limiter nor sedimentation changed the flux, $F=F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ and the cell work is all there
is (check line `[C2]`).

Summing $V_i$[^rg-a40f8bb06a7a] times @eq-ch06-cell-work over a closed column and adding the potential-energy change
$\sum_iV_i\phi_i\dot\rho_i$ gives the step's defect of $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$. Since the face form alone makes that
sum vanish (@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$), the defect is

$$
\mathcal D = \Delta t\sum_iV_i\big(W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i - W^{\mathrm{face}}_i[F^{\mathrm{ref}}]\big),
$$ {#eq-ch06-cell-defect}

The code forms this defect per stage, with the potential-energy change of the moved mass, as `gwfix_stage`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

per stage, before the stage weights of @sec-ch06-fixer. It does not telescope. The argument has four steps.

1. The face form books, per face $i+\tfrac12$, the mass $\Delta t\,A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}$ leaving cell $i$ at $\phi_i$[^rg-6f8cf364cedd] and
   entering cell $i+1$ at $\phi_{i+1}$ (@eq-ch06-dwork-face).
2. Summed over a closed column, each face therefore appears twice with opposite signs, and the face terms cancel to
   the two walls, where $F=0$ (@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$).
3. The cell form books $g_1m_{1,i}$ per cell. That is a cell quantity: no face value enters it, so no term of cell $i$
   has a partner of the opposite sign in cell $i\pm1$.
4. Hence $\sum_iV_i(W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i-W^{\mathrm{face}}_i[F^{\mathrm{ref}}])$ is a sum of unpaired terms, and it is
   zero only if the momentum profile happens to equal the face-flux average; @eq-ch06-cell-defect is that sum.

 `cellface_check.py` `[C2]` measures a defect of $1.6\times10^{-2}$ of $\sum_iV_i\lvert W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i\rvert$ on a
random closed column.

Locally the cell form is exact, in three steps:

1. The exact gravity work of cell $i$ is $g_1V_i\langle\rho v_1\rangle_{V_i}$ (@eq-ch06-dwork-template), and
   $\langle\rho v_1\rangle_{V_i}=m_{1,i}$, the conserved momentum the cell stores.
2. The primitive velocity is that momentum over the cell's total density: every equation of state at the pin divides
   the stored momentum by $\rho_i$, the dry plus all species densities (`IdealMoistImpl::_cons2prim`,
   {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_cons2prim >}}; likewise `MoistMixtureImpl`, and for `ideal-gas` the
   kernel sets the density from the conserved density and divides the momenta by it, `ideal_gas_cons2prim`
   [`ideal_gas_impl.h:16-24`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/ideal_gas_impl.h#L16-L24)).
   So $\rho_iv_{1,i}=m_{1,i}$ up to two roundings, the division and the product, at most $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$[^rg-d0b9cfeec328] relative,
   unless the equation-of-state limiter's density floor fires: `apply_primitive_limiter_` then raises the primitive
   density to the floor after the division, `clamp_min_`
   ([`equation_of_state.cpp:341`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L341)),
   and $\rho_iv_{1,i}\ne m_{1,i}$ in that cell.
3. Hence $W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i=g_1m_{1,i}$ at $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}=1$: the exact cell work of the stage state, to that
   round-off. With $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}<1$ the $G_i$ term is the hydrostatic split, not the cell work, and is not
   claimed exact.

What it gets wrong is the budget, @eq-ch06-cell-defect: the mass the faces move is booked at the cell centroids,
not where it crosses. `[C1]` and `[C2]` of `derivation_check.py` check the template identity and step 2.[^ch06-cell-chk]

[^ch06-cell-chk]: [sha: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/cellface_check.py`, CPU[^rg-7034ba898e85], double, 1 process;
    Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6; output identical to the committed file]. Output `cellface_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`.
    The port is line for line: the gravity-work block of `HydroImpl::forward` without the corrected-PE call, the cell
    work of `ConstGravityImpl::forward` and `radial_centers`. `derivation_check.py`, output `derivation_check.out`,
    lines `[C1]`–`[C2]`, with sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The forcing runs inside the stage, with the other forcings, on the primitive state of the stage start, and its
increment is scaled by $\Delta t$[^rg-88e66c6f06bb] like every other term, in the loop over `forcings`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
Everything is a cell average; the body force and its work are pointwise in each cell, with no stencil, so walls,
seams and ghosts play no part. The face part of @eq-ch06-cell-work reads the two $x_1$ faces of the cell and is
computed after the $x_1$ flux is final, that is after the positivity limiter and sedimentation. With an implicit
scheme the vertical implicit operator linearises the same cell work (@sec-ch06-vic). @fig-ch06-cell-defect shows
the per-cell term whose sum is @eq-ch06-cell-defect.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-cell-defect
#| fig-cap: "Per-cell contribution V(W^cell - W^face) to the E + PE_d defect of the cell form, on a random closed 24-cell column (nondimensional, g_1 = -10, one stage of length 0.01). The bars do not cancel: their sum is the defect the gravity-work fixer removes."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of 24 vermillion bars of both signs along x1 from 0 to 1, with a horizontal zero line."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch06.figures.fig_cell_defect import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**A minimal input.**

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8            # m s^-2, along x1
    gravity-work: cell     # the default is face; cell must be set
    # gravity-work-fixer defaults to true with cell
```

The `gravity-work` keys need a build at the pin ([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)); an older PyPI release
refuses them with "unknown key 'forcing/const-gravity/gravity-work'".

**What the parser refuses, and why.** `ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) applies, in this order:

1. *An unknown key* in `const-gravity`: only `grav1`, `grav2`, `grav3`, `non-hydrostatic`, `gravity-work`,
   `gravity-work-fixer` are accepted, so a misspelt key is an error.
2. *`non-hydrostatic` outside $[0,1]$*: $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$ is a split fraction.
3. *`gravity-work` other than `cell`, `face-wallc`, `face`*: there are only three forms. `HydroImpl::reset` checks the
   same again, so construction from Python agrees ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch06-cell-work.** The first term is added by the forcing
({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
du[IVX] += dt * w[IDN] * options->grav1() * options->non_hydrostatic();
du[IPR] += dt * w[IDN] * w[IVX] * options->grav1() * options->non_hydrostatic();
```

The second line is $\Delta t\,\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}\rho_iv_{1,i}g_1$. The $G_i$ term is added by the hydrostatic
correction, `du[IPR] += dt * w[IVX] * rho_grav * (1 - non_hydrostatic)`, and the face work of $F-F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ as
`gravity_energy_correction`, both in `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| keys and defaults | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `from_yaml` | `const-gravity` |
| body force and cell work | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | `grav1` |
| cell mode flag | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `gw_cell` | `gravity-work` |
| Riemann flux kept | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `bflux1` | `gravity-work` |
| face work of $F-F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `vertical_mass_flux1` | `gravity-work` |
| hydrostatic part | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `rho_grav` | `non-hydrostatic` |
| setup checks | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |

: Code map of the constant gravity and the cell form. {#tbl-ch06-cell-code}

1. In `from_yaml`, read `grav1`..`grav3` (default 0), `non-hydrostatic` (default 1, refused outside $[0,1]$) and
   the work mode `gravity_work`, which defaults to `face`
   ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. Default `gravity-work-fixer` to true with `cell`, and refuse it with a face form when $g_1\neq0$, in
   `gravity_work_fixer` ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
3. In `forward`, add the body force and the cell work, the $x_1$ part scaled by `non_hydrostatic`
   ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward >}}).
4. Keep the Riemann mass flux as `bflux1` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. Book the face work of the rest as `gravity_energy_correction` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

The messages a user can hit are "forcing/const-gravity/gravity-work must be cell, face-wallc or face" and
"forcing/const-gravity/gravity-work-fixer needs gravity-work: cell".

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` | cell without fixer drifts | $>10^{-10}$ | planted control |
| `test_forcing.release` | total energy against boundary flux | $10^{-9}$ abs. | test threshold |

: Tests of the cell form; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run. {#tbl-ch06-cell-tests}

`[C2]` of `cellface_check.py` measures the defect of @eq-ch06-cell-defect and confirms that with $F=F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ the
cell mode books no face work; `[C2]` of `derivation_check.py` is step 2 of the exactness argument.

The arm "cell, fixer false" of `test_gravity_work_fixer` requires the $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ drift to exceed 100 times
`TOL` $=10^{-12}$, so the defect @eq-ch06-cell-defect is shown to be real and the fixer load-bearing
({{< code tests/test_gravity_work_fixer.py main >}}). `vertical_gravity_work_uses_continuity_mass_flux` checks the
total-energy change against the boundary flux to $10^{-9}$ ({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.vertical_gravity_work_uses_continuity_mass_flux >}}).
Both are registered with the corrected-PE switch off and run on CPU. Measured values at the pin are **missing
evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The cell form alone does not conserve $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$; with `gravity-work-fixer: false` the defect
@eq-ch06-cell-defect accumulates.
:::

- $g_2$ and $g_3$ book cell work only, whatever `gravity-work` says; the fixer refuses them.
- `non-hydrostatic` scales only the $x_1$ terms.
- Combinations with the study switches are listed in @sec-ch12-matrix; no moist cell-form budget test exists.

[^rg-cf144a647361]: const-gravity — constant-gravity forcing component

[^rg-f239edda6399]: forcing — forcing options block: a map with one sub-block per forcing component

[^rg-1186f06fe11f]: $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$ — non-hydrostatic factor in $[0,1]$: the fraction of gravity applied as a body force

[^rg-40de9bc874ef]: non-hydrostatic — fraction of the vertical body force retained by the non-hydrostatic treatment

[^rg-72cdee3ac795]: gravity-work — form of the $x_1$ gravity work: `face` (default), `face-wallc` or `cell`

[^rg-896a4d0cea2b]: x1max — upper bound of the first coordinate

[^rg-c40954ec43ff]: $W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i$ — cell form $\rho_iv_{1,i}g_1$

[^rg-7c89ae1f45ba]: $W^{\mathrm{face}}_i$ — face form $\tfrac{1}{V_i}[\phi_i\Delta_i[AF]-\Delta_i[A\phi F]]$

[^rg-82297cb4f780]: $F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ — the total $x_1$ mass flux as the Riemann solver returns it (dry plus every species row), before sedimentation and the positivity limiter change the flux; under `gravity-work: cell` only $F-F^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is booked as face work. Not a reference-state flux: the superscript is not the hydrostatic $\mathrm{ref}$ of §6 (the code comment writes $F^R$) [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$]

[^rg-b660c0a73eb0]: $\mathcal D$ — the $E+\mathrm{PE}_d$ defect of a step, the quantity the gravity-work fixer removes [J]

[^rg-88e66223cc5e]: grav1 — gravity component along the first coordinate

[^rg-a40f8bb06a7a]: $V_i$ — cell volume

[^rg-6f8cf364cedd]: $\phi_i$, $\phi_{i\pm1/2}$ — $\phi$ at the centroid and at the faces

[^rg-d0b9cfeec328]: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}$ — machine epsilon of the working precision (never bare $\epsilon$, which is $\epsilon_{\mathrm{piv}}$); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L11-L14)

[^rg-7034ba898e85]: CPU — central processing unit

[^rg-88e66c6f06bb]: $\Delta t$ — the step
